key_insight: Instead of building equivariant architectures, map each sample to a canonical orbit representative (canonical pose/order) and train a standard, unconstrained diffusion model on those canonicalized samples—recovering symmetry-invariant generation via canonicalization and inverse mapping.
problem_solved: Generative modeling of data with group symmetries (e.g., permutation of graph nodes, rotation/translation of 3D structures) without the complexity and engineering cost of designing equivariant networks or symmetry-aware priors.
method: Canonicalization: deterministically map each training sample to a unique orbit representative (fixed pose/order) that removes symmetry degrees of freedom.
Standard diffusion training: train an off-the-shelf, non-equivariant diffusion model on the canonicalized dataset.

Decanonicalization at sampling: generate canonical samples with the diffusion model and map them back to the original symmetry class (apply appropriate group action) to obtain valid, invariant outputs for tasks such as molecular graph generation.
impact: This approach simplifies model design and implementation while preserving symmetry invariances, making diffusion-based generative modeling for chemistry and other symmetry-rich domains more practical, modular, and scalable for practitioners.
visual_elements: Orbit diagram: many symmetric variants of a sample mapped to a single canonical representative (circle of states -> one highlighted canonical point).
Pipeline flowchart: Input data -> Canonicalization -> Standard Diffusion Model (train) -> Sample -> Decanonicalization -> Symmetric outputs.
Before/After molecular examples: raw molecule with arbitrary atom order/pose vs canonicalized representation and final generated molecule in physical pose.
Bar/complexity chart: comparison of engineering complexity and modularity between canonicalization + standard diffusion vs equivariant architectures.
paper_title: Rethinking Diffusion Models with Symmetries through Canonicalization with Applications to Molecular Graph Generation
paper_authors: Cai Zhou, Zijie Chen, Zian Li, Jike Wang, Kaiyi Jiang
